newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A two-hour flurry during the morning session proved to be the only excitement in what turned out to be a dull day on South Africa's currency market on Wednesday.
The rand settled at 4.6600/6050 against the dollar after trading in a 4.6630 to 4.6380 range during the day and from 4.6515/6565 at Tuesday's finish.
"We had a bit of a flurry for the first two hours and then it went dead," a dealer said.
"At the opening we went down on offshore selling," he said. "Then the offshore guys came and bought everything back and more." Local importers were also seen in the hunt for dollars.
Dealers said that after popping above the 4.66 level, the rand ran into dollar selling interest, which kept it in a tight range for the rest of the day.
"There seems to be large selling interest above 4.66," another trader said, adding that it was unclear whether the selling interest was local or offshore.
Against the crosses, the rand made healthy gains against sterling after cable retraced to below 1.64 in early New York trade on Thursday.
Cable's retracement from above 1.68 began on Tuesday after comments by British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke who said the pound's recent strength was beginning to worry British business.
The rand was last quoted at 7.6331/6459 against sterling from 7.7310/7416 overnight.
Against the mark, the rand was little changed at 0.3349/3355 from 0.3355/3359 overnight.
On the bond market, bonds ended what dealers described as a desparately quiet day little changed.
The key R150 was last pegged at a 15.82 percent yield from 15.795 percent overnight.
"It has been absolutely dead," a trader said. Interest was limited to small amounts of local jobber selling with offshore nibbling at the higher levels.
On the money market, all of South Africa's "big four" banks held their three-month NCD rates at 17.10 percent offered, while 90-day BAs were also steady in a 16.40 to 16.65 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage up at 9.436 billion rand on Tuesday from 8.482 billion rand on Monday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net buyers of local bonds worth 378.05 million rand on Tuesday after buying 49.76 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 5.87 billion rand on Tuesday from 3.28 billion rand on Monday.
